    "### Scoring"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "6bdb22af",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The tmol score function is based on the Rosetta energy function. The score function is composed of many terms and weights for those terms. The default score function terms and weights are set to match the beta2016_cart score function from Rosetta3.\n",
    "\n",
    "Generally, you want to optimize a structure before interpreting its score closely -- a freshly-loaded crystal structure often has small clashes an optimizer would remove."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f86e5caf",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "#### Scoring a PoseStack"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "622e34e8",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The simplest way to score a PoseStack is with the whole_pose_scoring_module, which will return a tensor with one score for each structure in the stack `[nposes]`."

   "source": [
    "Torsion-space minimization moves internal degrees of freedom (bond torsions) instead of raw xyz coordinates, following a `FoldForest` -- the kinematic tree describing how motion at one bond propagates through the rest of the structure. It reuses the same coordinate gradients as above, reparameterized through that tree; the Advanced Kinematics notebook covers FoldForests in depth, so here we just build the default one.\n",
    "\n",
    "`tmol.MoveMap` says which internal degrees of freedom are allowed to move; `move_all_named_torsions = True` with jumps left off moves every named torsion (phi/psi/chi) and nothing else."

    "# Cartesian gradients\n",
    "print(\"Cartesian\")\n",
    "coords = pose_stack.coords.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)\n",
    "whole_scorer(coords).sum().backward()\n",
    "atom_grad = torch.nan_to_num(coords.grad[0]).norm(dim=-1)\n",
    "for atom in atom_grad.topk(10).indices.tolist():\n",
    "    print(f\"{atom_label(pose_stack, 0, atom)}: {float(atom_grad[atom]):.3f} per A\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Torsion gradients: forward kinematics (dofs -> coords) feeding the scorer\n",
    "print(\"Torsion\")\n",
    "kin_module = PoseStackKinematicsModule(\n",
    "    pose_stack, tmol.FoldForest.reasonable_fold_forest(pose_stack)\n",
    ")\n",
    "kin_network = KinForestSfxnNetwork(score_function, pose_stack, kin_module)\n",
    "kin_network().sum().backward()\n",
    "dof_grad = torch.zeros_like(kin_network.full_dofs)\n",
    "dof_grad[kin_network.dof_mask] = kin_network.masked_dofs.grad\n",
    "\n",
    "labels, nodes = torsion_labels(pose_stack, kin_module, 0)\n",
    "torsion_grad = dof_grad[nodes.to(dof_grad.device), BondDOFTypes.phi_c]\n",
    "for i in torsion_grad.abs().topk(10).indices.tolist():\n",
    "    print(f\"{labels[i]}: {float(torsion_grad[i]):.3f} per radian\")"

    "### Relax"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "119e87d6",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "`tmol.fast_relax` alternates packing and minimization over a multi-stage schedule, instead of running either once. It needs a `PackerPalette`, a movemap, and a `FoldForest`, all already introduced above."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "3b5a1532",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "#### Relax options (cycles, schedule)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a9dd5f8e",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "`num_repeats` controls how many times the full schedule runs; `schedule` is a list of stages, each ramping `fa_rep` (and, if constraints are active, their weight) from mild to full strength -- packing near-clashing structures directly at full repulsive weight tends to get stuck. Omit `schedule` for the built-in default schedule."
   ]
